question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y),\, & 0\le x\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\le \frac{\pi }{4}).$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}\},$ and the event $A=\{X\le \frac{\pi }{4}\}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14215348/assets/ea585fb6e12672f5cc854578cb12ff0357cfcd8d2f3d3b75a82723241cdaf3d4.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le \frac{\pi }{4}) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{x}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{x}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)]_{y=x}^{y=\pi /2}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{2})]}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-0+1 \\  & =\frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & ≈0.793.\end{aligned}
$$
